learning_outcomes.text: Classifies engineering materials and analyzes their deformation, fracture, and mechanical behavior from an engineering perspective.
Plans, implements, and interprets destructive testing (tensile, compressive, bending, hardness, impact, fatigue, creep, etc.) tests according to standards.
Prepares and examines the microstructure of materials using metallographic methods and relates it to mechanical properties.
Compares non-destructive testing methods and selects the appropriate testing method for different engineering applications.
Analyzes data obtained from material tests, uses them in solving engineering problems, and presents them in a technical report.

syllabus_topics: Classification of Materials, Overview of Engineering Materials (metals, polymers, ceramics, composites)
Deformation and Fracture of Materials, Elastic-plastic deformation, Types of Fracture
Purpose and Importance of Material Testing, Comparison of Destructive and Non-Destructive Testing Methods
Tensile Test, Stress-strain diagram, Determination of Mechanical Properties
Hardness Tests, Brinell, Rockwell, Vickers, Microhardness methods
Impact Test (Charpy-Izod), Energy absorption and toughness
Metallographic Examination, Sample preparation, etching, microstructure Analysis
Non-destructive testing methods, Visual Inspection (VT), Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT), Eddy Current Testing (ET)
Ultrasonic Testing (UT), Phased Array Ultrasonic Testing (PAUT)
Radiographic Testing (RT), Acoustic Emission Testing (AE), General evaluation and application examples
